item.title: US flight cancellations: Air India issues advisory amid outage; here’s how you can check if your flight is impacted
item.description: Air India has issued a travel advisory amid widespread flight disruptions across the US following a communications outage. Passengers travelling to and from the country have been advised to check their flight status online before heading to the airport.
item.dc:creator: Swati Gandhi
item.content:encoded: Air India on Saturday issued a travel advisory following widespread flight disruptions across the United States due to a communications outage. The airline advised passengers to check the status of their flights departing from or arriving at airports across the country.In a social media post, the Indian carrier wrote, "A nationwide ground stop is currently in effect across the US due to communication outages affecting air traffic operations. As a result, departures from airports across the U.S. are impacted, with possible consequential disruptions to Air India flights to and from the U.S. Passengers are advised to check the latest status of their flights and plan their journey to the airport accordingly."It added, “Our teams continue to closely monitor the situation and will share updates as available.”Why are airports across the US seeing disruptions?On Friday (local time), US authorities halted flights nationwide for the longest period since the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, highlighting vulnerabilities in the country's air traffic control system, Bloomberg reported.The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) announced a ground stop covering airports across the country in an advisory posted on its website on Friday afternoon. It stated that all departing traffic would remain halted until further notice. The agency later attributed the disruption to a temporary telecommunications outage.The FAA said, "Every flight has been accounted for, and international flights will be handled on a case-by-case basis." Although a handful of international flights were allowed to depart a few hours after the grounding began, passengers were left stranded at airports across the country, roughly two weeks ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, with little clarity on when normal operations would resume.According to reports, the latest incident marks the third nationwide ground stop in US history, following a 2023 disruption involving the FAA's safety notification system for pilots and dispatchers and the September 11 terrorist attacks in 2001.With flight operations affected across the country, passengers travelling to or from the US may want to check whether their scheduled flights have been delayed or cancelled. Here's how to check your flight status online.How to check online if your flight is affectedHere is a step-by-step guide to checking whether your flight has been affected by the outage:1. Visit Air India's official website: www.airindia.com.2. Click on the 'Book and Manage' option on the homepage.3. Select 'Flight Status' from the drop-down menu.4. Enter your details. You can use your flight number, PNR, or route, along with your travel date.5. Click on 'Get Flight Status' to view the latest updates.Alternatively, you can visit Air India's Flight Status page (https://www.airindia.com/in/en/manage/flight-status.html) directly to check your flight details.

item.title: US Loses Measles Elimination Status as Cases Surge, WSJ Says
item.description: The US has lost its long-standing status as having eradicated measles after transmission of the disease has continued through the past year and broken case records, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing unidentified people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- The US has lost its long-standing status as having eradicated measles after transmission of the disease has continued through the past year and broken case records, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing unidentified people familiar with the matter.The report followed a review of the evidence by the Pan American Health Organization, which verifies nations’ elimination status. PAHO and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention weren’t immediately available to comment after normal business hours on Friday.PAHO evaluates whether a single strain of measles virus has been circulating in a community for 12 months. Utah’s outbreak — which has infected more than 700 people — met the criteria and cost the US its status. While the loss of the status is just a label, it does represent a national failure to control the highly contagious disease. It’s also likely to prompt warnings about travel to the US and vaccine advisories from other nations.Canada lost its status a year ago. To regain it, the countries must prove continuous transmission has stopped and that surveillance systems to track the disease have been strengthened. The US officially eliminated measles in 2000 following a public communications push. But vaccination rates declined as the pandemic increased distrust in federal health guidance, creating an opportunity for the virus to take hold again. The CDC has confirmed 5,412 cases so far in 2026, more than double last year’s total and the highest number recorded since 1991. Under Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the CDC has been upended by staff departures and leadership changes. About a third of the career staff were forced out or voluntarily left following cuts from Elon Musk’s so-called Department of Government Efficiency. The public health agency has also been overwhelmed with responding to other outbreaks, including Ebola and cyclosporiasis. In August, CDC Director Erica Schwartz became the agency’s first permanent director in almost a year. Continuous SpreadPennsylvania has seen the largest outbreak in the US this year, recording more than 1,500 cases since it began in April and reporting its seventh measles-related death on Friday. A total of nine people in the US have died from measles so far this year — three times the toll in 2025. The CDC has only recognized six of these deaths following a feud with Pennsylvania over how they were classified.But it was Utah’s cases that led to the loss of elimination status. The state’s outbreak began in June 2025 and has continued to grow. Its public health experts say the virus has likely infected more people than what’s been recorded by local health departments. Only 87.2% of Utah kindergartners were inoculated with the MMR vaccine in the 2025-2026 school year, according to the CDC. Kennedy, who previously led an anti-vaccine organization and said getting the measles, mumps and rubella shot should be a “personal choice,” has upended US inoculation policy alongside President Donald Trump. Trump issued an executive order earlier this year directing HHS to produce a report on how to split up the MMR vaccine into separate components, which could make it more time-consuming for Americans to get all three. It would also mean complicated and expensive retoolings for manufacturers Merck & Co. and GSK Plc. While no vaccine is perfect, the MMR vaccine is 97% effective in preventing disease after two doses, according to the CDC. Measles is highly contagious, infecting up to 90% of unvaccinated people exposed to the disease. People experience flu-like symptoms and a red rash all over the body, sometimes leading to complications including encephalitis, pneumonia and even death. --With assistance from Andrea Navarro and Andrea Chang.(Updates with additional details beginning in the fifth paragraph.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: US FAA grounds flights nationwide for second time since 9/11: What caused the disruption as 10,000 flights face delays?
item.description: The FAA grounded US flights nationwide after a telecommunications outage disrupted air traffic control centres. More than 10,000 delays were reported, with cancellations and diversions mounting. This was the second nationwide ground stop since 9/11.
item.dc:creator: Prabhakar Jha
item.content:encoded: The US aviation system faced an unprecedented disruption after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday, halting departing flights at airports across the country, AP reported.While a full investigation is pending and no exact cause has come to fore, various reports mention the cause to be a communications outage that is affecting air traffic control centres.The disruption affected thousands of flights, leaving passengers stranded at airports, forcing airlines to divert aircraft and disrupting international travel.This was the second time since the September, 2001 (9/11) terrorist attack in the US state of New York that flight operations across the country has been halted. Another nationwide outage was reported in 2023.The FAA said the decision was taken as a precaution to ensure flight safety while technicians investigated the problem. Here is what happened, how many flights were affected and what authorities have said about the cause:What happened in the US?The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday afternoon (local time), instructing airports to halt all departing traffic until further notice.According to multiple reports, the problem stemmed from a telecommunications outage affecting the 22 air route traffic control centres that manage aircraft travelling between airports across the US.The ground stop did not mean that aircraft already flying were ordered to land immediately. Flights that were airborne continued towards their destinations, with authorities coordinating their safe landing.How many flights were affected by the FAA's ground stop?The disruption affected thousands of flights across the US, with cancellations, delays and diversions mounting as the stoppage continued.According to aviation analytics company Cirium and cited by AP, at least 600 flights had been diverted as of 5.50 pm Eastern Time on Friday.Of these, 496 flights were sent back to the airports from which they had originally departed, while 104 were diverted to alternative airports. Chicago O'Hare International Airport, Denver International Airport, Dallas Fort Worth International Airport and Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport were among the airports receiving diverted aircraft.The scale of the disruption was expected to increase. Around 11,000 flights carrying more than 1.5 million passengers had been scheduled to depart US airports after 4 pm Eastern Time on Friday.Flight-tracking website FlightAware reported more than 10,000 delays and over 4,000 cancellations within a short period of the disruption.FlightRadar24 estimated that around 3,100 aircraft were airborne and headed towards US airports when the ground stop began.What caused the nationwide flight disruption?The FAA initially attributed the ground stop to a temporary telecommunications outage affecting air traffic control operations. However, the exact cause of has not established as of yet.A CBS News report, citing multiple sources, said an update to the private communications network connecting the US air traffic control system had triggered a system reboot, resulting in a crash and communications outage.According to reports, investigators are examining whether a software update could have triggered the outage.Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication that the incident was a deliberate attack or a threat to the US.How were international flights affected?The European aviation agency Eurocontrol suspended all US-bound departures from its 42 member states at the FAA's request, Reuters reported. The suspension was scheduled to run from 5 pm Eastern Time on Friday until midnight.Mexico's federal aviation agency also grounded scheduled flights departing Mexican airports for the US.Air India warned that the nationwide ground stop could have consequential effects on its flights to and from the US. In a statement, the airline advised passengers to check their flight status before travelling to the airport.Is this the first time the US has grounded all flights nationwide?The latest incident was the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023, when a malfunction in a key FAA computer system disrupted flight operations across the country.Before that, the last nationwide grounding occurred following the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.
